s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute tender nodule on the forehead with granulomatous inflammation and yeast infection
salient_findings: Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
Granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts
key_facts: 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
Treated with fingolimod for 3 years
Nodule on forehead gradually grew over 3 weeks
History of bumping forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
No fever, neck stiffness, or photophobia
Lives alone with a pet cat and spends minimal time outdoors
No recent exposure to systemic steroids
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Absolute CD4 count: 56/μL
HIV test: Negative
Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts and tissue culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans

shortlist.label: Sporotrichosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute tender nodule on the forehead with granulomatous inflammation, although less likely given the biopsy results

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the granulomatous inflammation, but less likely due to the specific yeast morphology and culture results

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the granulomatous inflammation, but less likely due to the specific yeast morphology and culture results

shortlist.label: Phaeohyphomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely, but still a consideration given the subacute presentation and granulomatous inflammation
